property.text: Block processing must enforce maximum block size limits (EIP-7934 RLP execution block size limit). Blocks exceeding the size limit must be rejected early in the validation pipeline before full deserialization.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends extremely large blocks via P2P. EIP-7934 provides a maximum RLP block size. Blocks exceeding this must be rejected before consuming resources.

property.severity_justification: Oversized blocks without early rejection cause memory exhaustion and CPU waste, potentially crashing nodes.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block exceeding EIP-7934 size limit that is not rejected early.

property.text: The bloom filter bit arithmetic must be implemented identically across all clients: bit_to_set = Uint.from_be_bytes(hash[idx:idx+2]) AND 0x07FF, bit_index = 0x07FF - bit_to_set, byte_index = bit_index // 8, bit_value = 1 << (7 - (bit_index % 8)). Any deviation produces a different bloom.

reachability.notes: Any client implementing bloom bit arithmetic differently will produce different bloom values, causing receipt root divergence. This is a cross-client consensus property.

property.severity_justification: Bloom arithmetic inconsistency across clients directly causes consensus splits on any block with non-empty logs.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a client computing bloom differently from the specification, causing receipt root mismatch.

property.text: Bloom filter collisions from adversarially crafted log addresses and topics must not cause excessive computational overhead beyond O(n) in the total number of log entries and topics, bounded by the block gas limit.

reachability.notes: Bloom filter collisions are inherent to the probabilistic design. Impact is limited to log query performance, not consensus. Gas limits bound computation.

property.severity_justification: Bloom collisions degrade query performance but do not affect consensus. Gas limits bound the attacker's ability to maximize collisions.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Known design limitation. Not a vulnerability unless it causes consensus-level impact.

property.text: Bloom filter computation must be bounded by EIP-7825 transaction gas limit cap and EIP-7934 block size limit. The total number of keccak256 calls in logs_bloom must not exceed (1 + max_topics_per_log) * max_logs_per_block.

reachability.notes: A block maximizing log output within gas limits produces the most bloom computation. Bounded by gas and block size limits.

property.severity_justification: Bloom computation is O(n) and bounded by gas limits. Known computational cost, not a vulnerability.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Known design property. Only relevant if computation exceeds implicit bounds.

property.text: Transaction type information leaked through receipt encoding prefix bytes (0x01-0x04) is a known, by-design property of EIP-2718. This information is publicly available on-chain and does not constitute a vulnerability.

reachability.notes: Transaction type is publicly observable on-chain. Receipt prefix bytes are part of the EIP-2718 specification.

property.severity_justification: By-design information disclosure. Transaction types are publicly visible on-chain.

property.text: Block proposer identity is cryptographically bound to the block via the consensus layer signature. Arbitrary data in extra_data (up to 32 bytes) is a known feature and does not constitute a repudiation vulnerability.

reachability.notes: Block proposer is identified via CL. extra_data is a known 32-byte field used for client identification and other purposes.

property.severity_justification: Known feature of the block header. No security impact from extra_data content.

property.text: The gas_used field in the header must not exceed the gas_limit field. A block with gas_used > gas_limit must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends block with gas_used exceeding gas_limit. If not validated, this violates fundamental gas accounting.

property.severity_justification: gas_used > gas_limit indicates a fundamentally invalid block. Accepting it would violate core protocol invariants.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate acceptance of a block where gas_used exceeds gas_limit.

property.text: The block header bloom field must equal the combined logs_bloom computed from all transaction receipts in the block. A mismatch between header bloom and computed bloom must cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends block with header bloom that does not match the combined receipt blooms. If not verified, incorrect bloom data propagates.

property.severity_justification: Header bloom mismatch indicates tampered or incorrect receipt data. Causes consensus divergence between validating and non-validating clients.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block with mismatched header bloom being accepted.

property.text: The parent_hash field in a block header must reference an existing valid block in the canonical chain. A block with an unknown or invalid parent_hash must be rejected or deferred.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends block with fabricated parent_hash. Must be validated against the local chain state.

property.severity_justification: Accepting a block with invalid parent_hash could cause the node to build on a non-existent chain, leading to fork choice confusion.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate acceptance of a block with an unknown parent_hash.

property.text: The timestamp in a block header must be strictly greater than the parent block's timestamp. A block with timestamp <= parent.timestamp must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends block with timestamp equal to or less than parent. If accepted, time-dependent logic (e.g., difficulty/base fee adjustments) breaks.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect timestamp ordering could disrupt time-dependent protocol logic and cause consensus divergence.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate acceptance of a block with non-increasing timestamp.
